en: The standard of The Macallan line, aged entirely in sherry barrels. It's perfect for people who want to enjoy The Macallan without breaking the bank.
It may be the standard bearer of the line, but it's guaranteed to deliver "The Macallan" taste! I recommend you experience its sweet, full flavor and aroma for yourself.
The Macallan distillery, nestled in the Scottish highlands, has a storied 190-year history of careful attention to detail.
Their Speyside single malt whiskies are crafted from carefully selected wheat, yeast, and the crystal-clear water of the Spey river.
This whisky's taste invokes the aroma of dried fruit and the sweetness of cherries.
You'll then feel the woodiness of the cask, followed by an aftertaste that invites vivid memories of toffee.
This 10-year scotch, born in a cherrywood cask, is meant for casual enjoyment.
The best-selling single malt whisky in the world, known for its light and fresh flavor.
Glenfiddich 12 Years is the best selling single malt whisky in the world. This bottle set the industry standard for a single malt. You'll find it light and fresh.
The nose is full of fruit, and it has a clean finish, making it exceptionally easy to drink.
Its light flavor makes it popular with the ladies and anyone new to single malt whiskies.
It has a slightly smoky flavor coupled with a ripe, fruity aroma. Its crisp aftertaste is also quite unique.
Since it was bottled without being overly chilled, you can still enjoy the flavors imparted by the aging process. I think it's considered a collector's item.
A 12-year-old Scotch whisky with ripe, floral overtones.
That's the standard of the Bowmore line. Sherry barrels give it its uniquely ripe, floral overtones. Seaweeds unique to Islay give it a distinctive flavor and saltiness.
These qualities have earned it the title "Queen of Islay." It stands a cut above the rest of the single malt 12-year-old whiskies.
This bottle is the pinnacle of Scotch whiskies, head and shoulders above the competition.
More than thirty different single malts aged over thirty years are hand selected for their mellow character and blended. Truly the king of blended whiskies.
You can enjoy the taste of this whisky that can only be achieved by thirty years of aging. The fact that only 2,500 cases are bottled each year makes it quite rare.
This is the ultimate blended whisky. It boasts a rich and smooth taste only made possible by combining over forty single malts.
This could very well be called the crown jewel of Ballantine's whisky blending skills. It's well loved the world over, to the point of some calling it <Italic>the</Italic> scotch.
It's safe to say this 10 year Laphroaig is the standard-bearer of the brand. It's characterized by an intensely smoky flavor and a smooth, dry body.
And it has more than its share of quirks, so most people either love it or hate it. If you end up loving this one, it'll be one drink you'll never forget.
This beer won Japan's first gold award in international competition, and then defended the title for the next two years. It's a premium beer by Japanese and world standards.
Unyielding commitment to quality ingredients and Suntory's years of brewing know-how produce a delicious, almost magical flavor.
A frosty glass of this beer while nibbling sashimi or enjoying a Blu-ray movie on your day off... Now that's what I call living.
One of Japan's premium brandies, this bestseller has won over countless people with its bright, fruity bouquet and smooth taste.
As for the name... V.S.O.P stands for Very Superior Old Pale. But you probably already knew that.
One of Japan's premium brands, known internationally for its mellow flavor.
This is a premium Japanese whisky that has won over whisky lovers around the world.
This whisky starts with a single malt aged in Japanese Mizunara oak and then blended with over thirty different, painstakingly selected single malts.
The mellow flavor produced by this process has earned it a gold prize in international competition.
The finish is particularly good.
This bottle is popularly given in gift exchanges. Not that I've ever been gifted one...
This eighteen-year-old Japanese whisky has earned the loyalty of an ever-increasing international following of Japanese whisky fans abroad.
Among all of Yamazaki's highly decorated repertoire, this whisky has received the most awards.
Profound, aged flavor, dry fruitiness imparted by the cherry wood cask...
And a fragrant hint of chocolate on your palate will leave you stunned by this full-bodied whisky.
You've got to try this world-renowned flavor for yourself.
Kakubin is probably the most popular whisky in Japan, wouldn't you agree? Some call it the father of Japanese whisky.
Its popularity shows no signs of waning,  even after seventy years on the market. It has a sweet aroma, depth, and full body.
The name Kakubin comes from its unique squared bottle shape.
In 1946, this whisky was born in Japan, sparking a boom in Western liquor production.
The "Torys bars" of the 1960s derive their namesake from this whisky, and contributed to the popularization of whisky.
Its brand mascot Uncle Torys was beloved for his humorous and somehow nostalgic appearance.
Torys Extra continues the legacy of Torys whisky, bringing a gentle and refreshing flavor to your palate.
It's the perfect base for a highball.
This is the standard of the Bowmore line. Sherry barrels give it its uniquely ripe, floral overtones. Seaweeds unique to Islay give it a distinctive flavor and saltiness.
That's a standard Scotch, made from a blend of over forty varieties of single malts. Not too heavy, not too light. It's got a great balance to it.
And the price isn't too high, either. I recommend it to casual Scotch drinkers. It's also a nice intro to blended whiskies, if you've never tried them before.
The Kuromaru is an exquisite blend of two types of shochu-- one rich and strong and the other light and full of fruit aromas.
A unique variety of sweet potato from the Kagoshima region gives it a mild flavor and refreshing, clean finish.
A remarkable specimen from France. This one won a top prize in an international cognac competition.
A blend of grapes from the four finest crus in the Cognac region produces a full but smooth palate. You haven't tasted cognac until you've tried this one.
A prime example of Korean soju. A natural spring water base gives it a clean taste, while premium Korean barley gives it a mellow, rounded flavor.
It's not all that expensive, either. I'd say it offers excellent value for the price. I used to drink this all the time, and its taste is still as familiar as an old friend.
To me, this bottle of soju brings back a lot of fond memories.
That's an exceptionally well known vodka. It's the fastest growing vodka brand in the U.S. these days. The elegant bottle design evokes the vast blue skies of California.
Their unique process of repeated distillation and filtration gives it a pure, smooth flavor. Maybe that's the secret behind its popularity. Either way, I recommend it.
A rum sold by Suntory. Rum is produced from sugarcane which is wrung and refined into molasses.
The color, grade, and flavor of rum varies with the production process, and Suntory Rum Gold is an amber-colored medium-bodied rum.
It's frequently used as a cocktail base, and it's reasonably priced so it won't break the bank, but...
Rum-based cocktails tend to be sweet and go down easy, so drink responsibly.
Tobe
A limited-edition whisky made to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the Yamazaki distillery.
This is a whisky released by Yamazaki in 1984. It was created to commemorate the twenty-fifth anniversary of the Yamazaki brand.
Distilled and placed in barrels for aging in 1984, it is created from only the finest single malts. A symbol of 25 years of the Yamazaki brand.
This whisky is a blend of selected single malts aged in Japanese Mizunara oak barrels that are unique to the Yamazaki brand.
This imparts into the whisky its Asian flavor, known around the world as the epitome of Japanese whisky.
This 10-year scotch, born in a cherry wood cask, is meant for casual enjoyment.
Carlsberg is known for brewing lagers, but they licensed Suntory to create this draft beer using their own in-house technique.
Together, they've created Carlsberg's first draft beer, found only here in Japan.
It has an impressively clean taste that goes well with all sorts of food.
That's the gin drinker's gin, enjoyed in 170 countries the world over. It's popular straight up or in cocktails like the martini.
I'd bet any bar you walk into has at least one bottle of this gin. It's got a full juniper flavor, with a fresh citrus bite to it. I love to drink it as a gin and tonic.
Toru Kirihata
The champion of single malt whiskies.
The Macallan premium single malt is the champion of single malt whiskies. This 52 year old whisky made in 1946 wasn't put on the market until the new millennium in 1999.
The sherry and wood flavors that are characteristic of The Macallan are more subdued, giving it more of an Islay malt peatiness.
They say this was the result of a coal shortage right after World War II, when significant amounts of peat were used in the malting process.
Expensive and extremely rare, but you can almost taste the history behind it.
Since it was bottled without being overly chilled, you can still enjoy the flavors imparted by the aging process. I think it's considered a collector's item.
Herradura Tequila is a premium tequila, 100%% distilled from the blue agave plant.
The Plata variety is barrel-aged for 40 days, and Herradura's best-seller.
Tequila has come to stand alongside vodka, gin, and rum as the four pillars of the cocktail world.
Before it gained worldwide popularity in the 20th century, it was enjoyed in Mexico as a local liquor.
